opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running and growing the company — people, offices, professional fees and stock pay. Up from $138M a year ago as IREN scales its AI business.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of data centers, GPUs and equipment over their useful lives. IREN lists this inside operating expenses — it is not part of the $46M cost of revenue above.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing the AI cloud platform and services.

opex.name: Impairment of assets
opex.note: Writing down assets whose value has fallen — mainly older mining equipment.

opex.name: Gains & other operating income, net
opex.note: A gain, not a cost: an $8M gain on selling property and equipment plus $2M of other operating income, less $4M of other operating expenses — so this line reduced operating costs by $6M.

follow100Note: IREN spent about $2.15 for every $1 it took in this quarter, so the $100 view is scaled up accordingly — the loss was covered by cash raised earlier; it held $3.5B of cash at quarter end.
footerNote: IREN reports in whole USD millions. Its income statement lists depreciation and amortization inside operating expenses rather than in cost of revenue, so the gross profit step here ($182M) is revenue less the $46M cost of revenue IREN itself reports.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: Down 5% from $240M a year ago, as mining shrank faster than AI grew

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: Net loss per share, basic and diluted

kpis.label: AI Cloud revenue
kpis.note: 88% of all revenue, vs $7M a year ago

kpis.label: Cash
kpis.note: Cash and equivalents at September 30, plus $2.3B of restricted cash

oneTimers: The $28M unrealized loss on financial instruments is a non-cash mark-to-market charge (revaluing contracts at current prices); the same line was a $665M gain a year ago and swings sign with markets.
The $21M decrease in fair value of assets held for sale is a write-down of assets IREN plans to sell — largely mining-related — not a cash cost.
otherDetail: Other expense was $75M, net: $73M of finance costs on IREN's borrowings, a $28M unrealized (paper) loss on financial instruments and a $21M write-down of assets held for sale, plus $4M of foreign-exchange losses — partly offset by $51M of interest income on its cash.

segments.name: AI Cloud Services
segments.note: Renting out GPU computing power for AI training and inference (running trained models) — the business IREN is pivoting to. Up from just $7M a year ago.

segments.name: AI Cloud Lease
segments.note: Leasing AI data-center capacity to customers under lease contracts — a brand-new revenue line this year.

segments.name: Bitcoin Mining
segments.note: Mining bitcoin in IREN's data centers — the old core business, being wound down as the company pivots to AI. Down from $233M a year ago.

takeaways.text: AI Cloud revenue was $200M — 88% of the total — vs $7M a year ago, split between cloud services ($135M) and leasing capacity ($65M, a new line). Bitcoin mining, a year ago effectively the whole company at $233M, fell 88% to $28M as IREN redirects power and data centers to AI.
takeaways.title: AI is now the business

takeaways.text: Delivering the service cost only $46M, leaving a $182M gross profit — an 80% margin. But running the company cost $368M, including $217M of selling, general and administrative costs and $148M of depreciation on its growing data-center fleet, turning that into a $186M operating loss.
takeaways.title: Huge gross margin, bigger overhead

takeaways.text: Below the operating line, $73M of finance costs and $49M of paper losses (a $28M unrealized loss on financial instruments and a $21M write-down of assets held for sale) were partly offset by $51M of interest income. A year ago those paper lines were a $665M gain and IREN made a $385M profit. It ended the quarter with $3.5B of cash to fund the build-out.
takeaways.title: Paper losses deepened the bottom line

verdict: IREN flipped its business in a year — AI cloud brought in $200M of its $228M revenue, up from just $7M, while bitcoin mining shrank to $28M — but the cost of the pivot produced a $263M net loss.
